title: Wan Renwang at the tea stall
summary: Out of the cave, Bi Yao asks Zhang Xiaofan to repay her by joining her sect; they argue over which side is sinful, and she leaves in anger. On Small Bamboo Peak, Shui Yue scolds Lu Xueqi for losing focus. At a roadside tea stall an old man calling himself Wan Renwang tells Xiaofan that the bead on his stick is Black Heart Elder's Blood-Striking Bead and that the stick is a demonic weapon. Xiaofan answers that he uses it to kill demons, so it is righteous, and the man vanishes. The man is the Ghost King: he meets Bi Yao, shows her the flower her mother gave him, takes her home, and plans to win Xiaofan over once the weapon has turned him into a killer. Xiaofan reaches a deserted town afraid of a Three-Tailed Fox. A fortune teller with a young granddaughter reads his face, warns that he is close to death, and takes four taels. Shi Tou, heir of the Jingang Sect, wants to kill the fox, and Xiaofan goes with him to the Black Stone Cave.

flags: Wan Renwang is shown as the Ghost King by the scene itself (651 s 'I've met Zhang Xiaofan'); EP19 opens with Xiaofan recognising him as 'the one in the tea stall'.
505 s 'Master. That rascal...' and 571 s 'Master.': the speaker addressing the Ghost King is not named, probably You Ji.
The fortune teller and the girl are not named in EP14-17 (she calls him 'Grandfather' in EP17); identified as Zhou Yixian and Xiao Huan from the novel.
362 s 'It's named Dementor': the English track's name for the soul-eating stick; 358 s 'Jiuyou Soul'. 466 s Xiaofan calls it the 'Fire Burning Stick' (the Fire Stick).
849 s: '10 taels' / '10 cash' are two overlapping lines; Xiaofan pays four taels.
